Use the Form pattern. - Only the whole page is busy, with no per-file status. Use `Progress` or `Spinner` alone. - The list of already-saved files is the whole screen. Use the Data table pattern. ## Decision rules - Offer two ways in, always: a `Button` ("Choose files") that opens the native picker, and a drop area. The Button is the accessible path; dropping is an extra, never the only way. - State the limits before the user picks (accepted types, maximum size, maximum count) as helper text in the drop area. Check them on selection and reject a file at once with its reason; do not start an upload you know will be refused. - One `ListItem` per file in a list, in the order chosen. Media is a file-type `icon`, the title is the file name, the description carries status text, and the action is the one control that applies to the current status. - Status drives the row, in this order: - queued or uploading: `Progress` with `value`, `valueLabel` ("42%") and the file name as `aria-label`; the action is "Cancel" (`Button variant="ghost"`, `iconOnly`). - uploading with unknown size: `Progress` with `indeterminate`. - done: description "Uploaded", a `Badge variant="success"`; the action is "Remove". - failed: description states the cause and what to do ("Upload failed. Check your connection and try again."), a `Badge variant="danger"`; the action is "Retry" (`Button variant="outline" size="sm"`), then "Remove". - Classify the failure like Error recovery does. The request failed (network, timeout, 5xx): offer Retry. The file is the problem (too large, wrong type, rejected by the server): no Retry, because the same file fails again; offer Remove and say what to change. - Retry re-uploads that file only: it keeps its place in the list, resets its progress to 0, and shows `loading` on the Retry Button. Other files are not touched, and successful files are never re-sent. - When two or more files failed, add one `Alert variant="danger"` above the list with a "Retry all" action for the retryable ones. One failed file needs only its own row. - Never clear the list because an upload failed. Failed files stay until the user retries or removes them. - Removing an uploaded file that is already saved is destructive; confirm with an `AlertDialog`. Removing a failed or queued file needs no confirmation. - Upload starts when files are chosen unless the surrounding form submits them; in a form, the form's submit is blocked while any file is uploading and the reason is said. - Wording: use the file name, say what happened, no "Oops". Do not show raw error codes as the message. ## Components and variants - `Button` variant: `primary`, `outline`, `ghost` · size: `sm`, `md` - `ListItem` variant: `outline` · size: `md` - `Progress` - `Badge` variant: `success`, `danger` · size: `sm` - `Alert` variant: `danger` · size: `md` ## Layout and density - Drop area on top, full width of the content column, with the Choose files Button and the limits text centred inside it; the file list sits directly below with `--atlas-spacing-3` between rows. - Use the same `ListItem` variant and size for every row. Titles stay on one line and truncate in the middle of the name, keeping the extension visible. - The drop area is a dashed `--atlas-border-strong` region on `--atlas-background-subtle`; while a file is dragged over it, switch the border to `--atlas-primary` and the fill to `--atlas-background-muted`. This is local composition, not a component; log it as a candidate if it recurs. ## Hierarchy and composition - Drop area → limits text → (summary Alert when several failed) → file list → the form's own actions. - Typography: the drop-area prompt takes `--atlas-text-body`; limits and status text take `--atlas-text-body-sm` in `--atlas-foreground-muted`.
